results.evidence: gate.suppress normalizes the email, defaults source to SUPPRESS_SOURCE ('suppress'), inserts one row with added_at=now, and the CLI prints 'suppressed <norm>' and exits 0. --source is wired through argparse and stored, and a blank source falls back to the default. tests/test_suppress.py pins utc_now to NOW and asserts the output 'suppressed alice@example.com', one row with email_norm alice@example.com, reason 'asked by phone', source 'suppress' and added_at NOW, and source 'phone call' with --source. All 10 tests in tests/test_suppress.py passed. I did not re-run the CLI by hand because the policy gate blocked the scratch-DB writes. I did not check that NOW equals 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z, so the test's NOW constant was not compared to the AC value.

gate.suppress selects the existing row and, if found, rolls back and returns added=False with the stored reason and added_at. It never updates the row. SuppressResult.line() then prints 'X already suppressed since <local date> (<reason>)'. The cli _run_suppress prints that line and returns EXIT_OK. tests/test_suppress.py::test_an_existing_entry_is_reported_and_left_unchanged pins now to 2026-12-01Z, suppresses with reason 'asked by phone', then re-suppresses with reason 'other'. It asserts the output 'alice@example.com already suppressed since 2026-11-30 (asked by phone)' and that the whole row (reason, source, added_at) is identical before and after. All 10 tests in tests/test_suppress.py pass.

The AC is item 3 in /Users/carlos/src/cottonwood-contractors-growth-engine/work/tasks/CCGE-120.md. gate.suppress normalizes the email first. A ValueError becomes GateError('email', ...), which prints 'error: email: ...'. A blank reason then fails _required('reason') with GateError, which prints 'error: reason: must not be empty'. Both checks run before the INSERT, so nothing is stored. cli._run_suppress catches GateError, prints 'error: ...' to stderr and returns EXIT_REFUSED, which is 1 (cli.py:36). test_refusals_store_nothing in tests/test_suppress.py covers all six cases from the AC: reason '  ', and addresses '  ', 'alice', 'a@b@c', '@example.com' and 'alice@'. For each it asserts exit 1, exactly one stderr line with the expected prefix, and an empty suppression table. I ran `pytest tests/test_suppress.py` and all 10 tests passed, including the 6 refusal cases.

tests/test_suppress.py::test_a_suppressed_address_is_honored_by_import_and_set_eligibility runs suppress on alice@example.com with reason x. It then runs prospects-import on a record with ALICE@example.com. That import exits 0 and the contact's eligibility is 'ineligible'. set-eligibility to eligible then exits EXIT_REFUSED. The test file passes (10 passed). The implementation matches the test. prospects.py:464-468 sets a new contact ineligible when its address is suppressed. eligibility.py:103 and :137-143 refuse eligible for a suppressed address.
